record.original_question: A function f (z) analytic in D is said to be typically real if f (z) is real, when and onlyPwhen z is real, see Rogosinski [668]. If f (z) = z + ∞ n n=2 an z is typically real in D, then z f (z) = P (z), 1 − z2 where P (0) = 0, Re P (z) > 0 in D. What other conditions must P (z) satisfy to make f (z) univalent in D?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{D}=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|<1\}$ denote the open unit disk. A function $f$ analytic in $\mathbb{D}$ is called typically real if, for $z\in\mathbb{D}$, $f(z)$ is real if and only if $z$ is real. Suppose
$$f(z)=z+\sum_{n=2}^{\infty}a_n z^n$$
is typically real in $\mathbb{D}$. It is known that one may write
$$\frac{z\,f(z)}{1-z^2}=P(z),$$
where $P$ is analytic in $\mathbb{D}$ with $P(0)=0$ and $\operatorname{Re} P(z)>0$ for all $z\in\mathbb{D}$.

Determine necessary and sufficient additional conditions on the function $P(z)$ which guarantee that $f(z)$ is univalent (one-to-one) in $\mathbb{D}$.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not surface a definitive characterization of those analytic functions $P$ with $P(0)=0$ and $\operatorname{Re} P>0$ for which the corresponding typically real function $f(z)=(1-z^2)P(z)/z$ is univalent in $\mathbb{D}$. Standard references on univalent functions discuss the typically real class and the Rogosinski representation, but do not appear to provide a complete additional condition on $P$ characterizing univalence; the status of the problem is therefore not clearly resolved from the available evidence.

status_evidence.title: Univalent Functions - P. L. Duren
status_evidence.snippet: Standard reference treating the class of typically real functions and Rogosinski's representation, without giving a complete extra condition on P forcing univalence.
status_evidence.claim: The classical theory describes the representation P(z)=zf(z)/(1-z^2) but does not single out a known necessary and sufficient extra condition for univalence.

status_evidence.title: Coefficient characterizations and sections for some univalent functions
status_evidence.snippet: Studies coefficient conditions for various subclasses of univalent functions including typically real functions.
status_evidence.claim: Recent literature on subclasses of typically real univalent functions does not present a definitive complete characterization of P.
